'''''Kalanchoe tomentosa''''', also known as the '''panda plant''', '''pussy ears''', or '''chocolate soldier''',<ref name="nparks">{{cite web |title=''Kalanchoe tomentosa'' |url=https://www.nparks.gov.sg/florafaunaweb/flora/3/4/3449 |website=NParks Flora & Fauna Web |publisher=National Parks Board, Singapore |access-date=2026-04-08}}</ref><ref name="rhs">{{cite web |title=''Kalanchoe tomentosa'' panda plant |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/9701/kalanchoe-tomentosa/details |website=Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=2026-04-08}}</ref> is a species of [[succulent plant]] in the family [[Crassulaceae]]. A native of [[Madagascar]], it is widely cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]] due to its distinctive velvety, silver-green leaves with chocolate-brown markings. It has received the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name="rhs" />

==Description==
''Kalanchoe tomentosa'' is a slow-growing, evergreen, semi-woody perennial succulent [[subshrub]] with an erect growth form.<ref name="nparks" /><ref name="ncsu">{{cite web |title=''Kalanchoe tomentosa'' (Panda Plant) |url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/kalanchoe-tomentosa/ |website=North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox |publisher=NC State University |access-date=2026-04-08}}</ref> It can reach a height of {{convert|0.4|to|1|m|ft|abbr=on}} and a spread of up to {{convert|0.9|m|ft|abbr=on}},<ref name="nparks" /><ref name="rhs" /> though it typically remains smaller in cultivation, around {{convert|30|to|50|cm|in|abbr=on}}.<ref name="plantura">{{cite web |title=''Kalanchoe tomentosa'': location, care & propagation |url=https://plantura.garden/uk/houseplants/kalanchoe-tomentosa/kalanchoe-tomentosa-overview |website=Plantura |access-date=2026-04-08}}</ref> Young roots are red with white tips.<ref name="nparks" />

The most distinctive feature of the plant is its [[leaf|leaves]], which are thick, fleshy, and oval-shaped, typically measuring up to {{convert|9|cm|in|abbr=on}} in length.<ref name="rhs" /> The leaves are arranged opposite or in a loose rosette and are densely covered with fine, silvery-white to grayish hairs ([[trichome]]s), giving them a velvety or felt-like texture.<ref name="nparks" /><ref name="ncsu" /> The leaf margins are scalloped and tipped with a series of dark brown to rusty-red spots or a continuous chocolate-brown rim, a characteristic that inspired the common name "chocolate soldier."<ref name="nparks" /><ref name="plantura" /> In mature plants, young leaves appear whitish and erect, while older leaves become lighter green, less fuzzy, and more horizontal.<ref name="nparks" />

The flowers are small, tubular, and bell-shaped, measuring about {{convert|1|cm|in|abbr=on}} in length, and are borne in [[panicle]]s atop erect stalks that can reach up to {{convert|45|cm|in|abbr=on}} in height.<ref name="rhs" /><ref name="ncsu" /> Flower colors range from greenish-white to yellow-green, sometimes with brown or purple petal tips.<ref name="nparks" /><ref name="ncsu" /> In their natural habitat, they bloom between March and June; however, indoor plants rarely flower.<ref name="plantura" /><ref name="nparks" /> The fruit is a dry [[capsule (fruit)|capsule]] containing numerous small seeds.<ref name="nparks" />

==Taxonomy==
The species was first described by the British botanist [[John Gilbert Baker]] in 1882 in the ''Journal of Botany, British and Foreign'', based on collections made from east-central Madagascar.<ref name="powo" /><ref name="smith2023">{{cite journal |last=Smith |first=Gideon F. |date=2023 |title=Taxonomy and nomenclature of ''Kalanchoe tomentosa'' (Crassulaceae subfam. Kalanchooideae), a variable, completely hairy species from Madagascar |journal=Phytotaxa |volume=609 |issue=4 |pages=267–276 |doi=10.11646/phytotaxa.609.4.5}}</ref> The [[specific epithet (botany)|specific epithet]] ''tomentosa'' is derived from the Latin ''tomentosus'', meaning "covered with dense, matted hairs,"<ref name="ncsu" /><ref name="plantura" /> in reference to the plant's velvety foliage. A [[heterotypic synonym]], ''Bryophyllum triangulare'' <small>Blanco</small> (1845), has been rejected as a [[nomen utique rejiciendum|name to be rejected]].<ref name="powo" />

In a 2023 revision, Smith provided an amplified description of the species and designated an [[epitype]] to clarify the application of the name.<ref name="smith2023" /> The species is highly variable in leaf shape, hair density, and margin coloration, which has led to the description of numerous [[cultivar]]s.<ref name="smith2023" />

==Distribution and habitat==
''Kalanchoe tomentosa'' is [[endemic]] to east-central [[Madagascar]], where it grows primarily in the seasonally dry tropical [[biome]].<ref name="powo" /><ref name="ncsu" /> Its natural habitat consists of rocky, well-drained soils, often on granite outcrops, in arid and semi-arid regions.<ref name="plantura" />

==Cultivars==
Numerous cultivars have been developed, selected for variations in leaf size, shape, and coloration:<ref name="plantura" /><ref name="ncsu" />
* 'Chocolate Soldier' – The most common cultivar, featuring narrower, pale-colored leaves with a more uniform and thicker dark chocolate-brown margin. It is reportedly faster-growing and has a clumping habit.<ref name="ncsu" /><ref name="smgrowers">{{cite web |title=''Kalanchoe tomentosa'' 'Chocolate Soldier' |url=http://smgrowers.com/products/plants/plantdisplayPrintView.asp?plant_id=3970 |website=San Marcos Growers |access-date=2026-04-08}}</ref>
* 'Golden Girl' – Characterized by golden-yellow, fuzzy leaves that become more vibrant with increased sunlight exposure. It produces clusters of golden trumpet-shaped flowers.<ref name="worldofsucculents">{{cite web |title=''Kalanchoe tomentosa'' 'Golden Girl' |url=https://worldofsucculents.com/kalanchoe-tomentosa-golden-girl/ |website=World of Succulents |access-date=2026-04-08}}</ref>
* 'Teddy Bear' – Features rounder, chocolate-brown leaves densely covered with fuzz and almost black markings at the tips.<ref name="ncsu" />
* 'Cinnamon' – Has long, oval-shaped russet leaves that appear almost black when grown in full sun.<ref name="ncsu" />
* 'Nigra' – Exhibits extremely dark brown to nearly black leaf margins, which can be dotted or continuous.<ref name="plantura" />
* 'Rubra' – Displays a reddish hue, particularly pronounced along the leaf edges, with a golden-red shimmer.<ref name="plantura" />
* 'Black Tie' – Another dark-margined selection.<ref name="wikidata">{{cite web |title=''Kalanchoe tomentosa'' |url=https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q142606 |website=Wikidata |access-date=2026-04-08}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
''Kalanchoe tomentosa'' is widely cultivated as a [[houseplant]] and in [[rock garden]]s, [[container garden]]s, and [[succulent garden]]s in warm climates. It is prized for its attractive, tactile foliage and low-maintenance requirements.<ref name="nparks" /><ref name="ncsu" />

===Growing conditions===
The plant thrives in bright, indirect sunlight, though it can tolerate some direct sun; however, intense afternoon sun may cause leaf burn.<ref name="ncsu" /><ref name="thespruce">{{cite web |title=Chocolate Soldier Plant Profile |url=https://www.thespruce.com/chocolate-soldier-plant-profile-5024790 |website=The Spruce |access-date=2026-04-08}}</ref> Insufficient light results in leggy, elongated growth.<ref name="ncsu" />

A well-draining potting mix, such as a cactus or succulent mix, is essential to prevent root rot.<ref name="nparks" /><ref name="rhs" /> The plant prefers temperatures between {{convert|15|and|23|C|F}} and is not frost-hardy; it should be grown in USDA hardiness zones 9–11 or brought indoors during winter.<ref name="ncsu" /><ref name="chicagobotanic">{{cite web |title=''Kalanchoe tomentosa'' - Panda Plant |url=https://www.chicagobotanic.org/plant-information/plant-finder/kalanchoe-tomentosa-panda-plant |website=Chicago Botanic Garden |access-date=2026-04-08}}</ref>

===Watering and feeding===
Water should be applied thoroughly but infrequently, allowing the top {{convert|2.5|cm|in|abbr=on}} of soil to dry out completely between waterings.<ref name="nparks" /> Overwatering is a common cause of plant failure, leading to root rot and mushy leaves.<ref name="ncsu" /> During the winter dormancy period, watering should be reduced significantly.<ref name="rhs" /> Fertilization is generally minimal; a half-strength balanced liquid fertilizer can be applied monthly during the growing season.<ref name="nparks" />

===Propagation===
The species is easily propagated by stem or leaf cuttings.<ref name="nparks" /><ref name="plantura" /> Cuttings should be allowed to callus for one to two days before being placed in a well-draining potting mix. Seeds can also be used, sown at {{convert|19|to|21|C|F}} in early spring.<ref name="rhs" />

===Pests and diseases===
Common pests include [[mealybug]]s, [[aphid]]s, and [[spider mite]]s.<ref name="ncsu" /><ref name="rhs" /> Overwatering can lead to root rot, and high humidity may promote [[powdery mildew]] or rust.<ref name="rhs" /> Shriveled or wrinkled leaves typically indicate underwatering, while yellow or mushy leaves suggest overwatering.<ref name="ncsu" />

==Toxicity==
Like many species in the genus ''[[Kalanchoe]]'', ''K. tomentosa'' is toxic to cats and dogs, and mildly toxic to humans if ingested.<ref name="thespruce" /> It is recommended to keep the plant out of reach of pets and small children.<ref name="ncsu" />

==Common names==
The plant is known by many common names across different languages and regions:<ref name="plantaedb">{{cite web |title=''Kalanchoe tomentosa'' - common names |url=https://plantaedb.com/taxa/phylum/angiosperms/order/saxifragales/family/crassulaceae/genus/kalanchoe/species/kalanchoe-tomentosa |website=PlantaeDB |access-date=2026-04-08}}</ref>
* English: Panda plant, pussy ears, chocolate soldier, velvet leaf kalanchoe, plush plant, teddy bear cactus, cocoon plant<ref name="thespruce" />
* Chinese: 月兔耳 (yuè tù ěr, "moon rabbit ear") or 褐斑伽蓝 (hè bān qié lán)<ref name="plantaedb" />
* Dutch: Pandaplant<ref name="plantaedb" />
* Indonesian: Kaktus panda<ref name="plantaedb" />
* Polish: Żyworódka omszona<ref name="plantaedb" />
* Ukrainian: Каланхое повстисте<ref name="plantaedb" />

==Uses==
The plant is primarily grown as an [[ornamental plant|ornamental]] for its striking foliage. It is suitable for indoor containers, hanging baskets, rooftop gardens, and rockeries.<ref name="nparks" /> In its native Madagascar, there is a popular belief that when a panda plant flowers for someone, it is an indication of richness and prosperity for their household.<ref name="smgrowers" />

==Conservation==
As of 2026, ''Kalanchoe tomentosa'' has not been formally assessed for the [[IUCN Red List]]. However, it is listed as a species of "least concern" by the Angiosperm Extinction Risk Predictions project, though with low confidence.<ref name="powo" /> The species is widely cultivated and not considered threatened in the wild, though habitat loss in Madagascar could impact wild populations.
